developments.title: Grok Bot gains Outlook, Calendar, and OneDrive plugins
detail: Grok Bot now includes three new plugins that let the AI read, write, and act across Microsoft accounts. The Outlook plugin enables searching, reading, and sending email as well as contact lookup; the Calendar plugin supports listing, creating, updating, and canceling events; the OneDrive plugin allows browsing, searching, and reading files.
These plugins are publicly listed on x.ai’s bot plugin directory, confirming they are shipped and usable today.
developments.why_it_matters: Bots can now automate email handling, schedule management, and file access directly within Microsoft services, expanding practical AI‑driven workflow capabilities.

developments.title: CallScript Enables Deterministic Code Mode via JSON Plans
detail: CallScript is a new tool that lets a language model write a restricted subset of JavaScript, which is then parsed into a JSON execution plan instead of being run directly. The JSON plan can be deterministically approved, stored, and resumed later, allowing consecutive calls to reference intermediate values without round‑tripping through the model’s context.
developments.why_it_matters: By converting generated code into auditable JSON plans, CallScript provides a way to enforce permission handling and security checks before execution, reducing the risk of unsafe code execution.

developments.title: CivilizationBench benchmark released
detail: CivilizationBench is introduced as a new benchmark designed to evaluate frontier AI technology. The creator positions it as a litmus test for measuring AI labs.
developments.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized way to compare AI labs' capabilities today.

developments.title: Muse Code exits beta, supports larger engineering tasks
detail: Muse Code has left its beta phase and is now engineered to handle bigger, more complex software development tasks. The tool can be installed with a single command line invocation, allowing developers to start using it immediately.
The announcement highlights that Muse Code is ready for production workloads, expanding its applicability beyond early testing scenarios.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can now rely on Muse Code for substantial engineering projects, gaining immediate access via a one‑command install, which accelerates adoption and real‑world usage.

developments.title: Abliteration.ai releases abliterated-model-large-v2
detail: Abliteration.ai announced the release of abliterated-model-large-v2, a new large language model built on GLM‑5.3. The model is US‑hosted, runs in FP8 precision, and offers a 1 million token context window with zero input/output prompt retention.

According to the announcement, the model is designed for offensive cyber, red‑team, and agent‑testing tasks that other models avoid, providing capabilities for cyber exploitation and security research.
developments.why_it_matters: The model gives security researchers immediate access to a high‑capacity, US‑hosted LLM for red‑team operations and agent testing, expanding the toolset for offensive cyber work today.

developments.title: DeepSeek v4 Flash vision implementation completed
detail: DeepSeek v4 Flash experimental with vision is now running fast on an M5 Max computer, analyzing images locally. The implementation for Metal, CUDA, and ROCm back‑ends is finished and only final tests remain before release.
developments.why_it_matters: The finished GPU back‑end support lets developers run DeepSeek v4 Flash vision models locally on Apple, NVIDIA, and AMD hardware today, expanding fast, on‑device AI capabilities.

developments.title: AmpCode adds live video chat to its shared space tab
detail: AmpCode has shipped live video chat for orbs and threads inside a new shared 'space' tab, letting teammates enter a collaborative room and talk in real time.
The feature is available now within AmpCode, turning the tool's existing workspace surface into a live meeting space rather than requiring a separate conferencing app.
developments.why_it_matters: Teams using AmpCode can now hold synchronous discussions in the same interface where their AI coding agents and threads already live, removing context-switching to external chat tools.

developments.title: Opencode Team Chat Plugin Adds Image Sending Capability
detail: The Opencode team chat plugin now supports sending images directly within chat sessions. The update was announced by the development team, noting that the feature works over SSH connections, though image blocks may still appear for some users.
developments.why_it_matters: Enabling image sharing improves collaboration for remote developers who rely on SSH, allowing richer communication without switching tools.

developments.title: Perplexity adds hybrid compute to Mac app for on‑device processing
detail: Perplexity announced a hybrid compute feature for all users of its Mac application, allowing the client to run local language models directly on the Mac.
The on‑device execution is aimed at agent steps that involve sensitive data such as medical records, tax returns, or litigation documents, keeping those files private.
developments.why_it_matters: By processing private files locally, users can avoid sending sensitive information to cloud servers, enhancing data privacy and security.

developments.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1
detail: Anthropic announced the launch of Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, billing them as the world’s most advanced models for coding and knowledge work and noting improvements in speed, intelligence, cost, and conversational tone.
Commentary notes that Claude Fable 5.1 can interpret brief, loosely worded requests and automatically fill in missing steps, a capability highlighted by Alex Albert.
developments.why_it_matters: The new models are now publicly available, giving developers access to more capable AI for coding and knowledge‑work tasks.

developments.title: Anthropic restricts mid‑conversation model switches for new organizations
detail: Anthropic announced that new organizations cannot switch models mid‑conversation; attempting to do so results in an error and loss of reasoning state. The change is currently limited to newly created accounts while existing users retain the previous behavior.
developments.why_it_matters: The restriction forces developers to commit to a single model per session, impacting workflows that rely on dynamic model selection and potentially increasing latency or complexity for multi‑model applications.

developments.title: ChatGPT desktop app bundles LibreOffice
detail: The ChatGPT desktop application, formerly known as Codex, was observed to include a full copy of the LibreOffice open‑source office suite. The LibreOffice files are stored in a hidden directory under ~/.cache.
The inclusion was discovered by Simon Willison, who shared a screenshot of the hidden folder showing the LibreOffice binaries alongside the ChatGPT client.
developments.why_it_matters: The hidden LibreOffice bundle increases disk usage for ChatGPT users and may expose unexpected software components, raising concerns about storage efficiency and potential security implications.

developments.title: Claude Fable 5.1 delivers benchmark wins and cost efficiency gains
detail: Claude Fable 5.1 shows measurable gains in performance and efficiency over prior Claude models. Fable 5.1 Low outperforms Mythos 5 High on Terminal-Bench 4.0, while running at approximately half the cost per performance compared to Fable 5 on CursorBench.

Cache reads are 25% more cost-efficient on the average task and up to 45% more cost-efficient on long-horizon agentic tasks. The release is also noted for producing coherent conversational output rather than the incoherent responses associated with prior versions.
developments.why_it_matters: Fable 5.1 Low beats Mythos 5 High on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and Fable 5.1 as a whole halves cost per performance versus Fable 5, with the largest cache-read savings on long-horizon agentic tasks.

developments.title: Tamagotchip: Native LLM Agent for ESP32
detail: The Tamagotchip project releases version 0 of a native LLM‑driven agent that runs on ESP32 hardware. The agent plans actions using a language model, executes them via Lua scripts, and requires a physical button as a permission system. The source code is available on GitHub, allowing developers to flash the firmware onto their devices.
developments.why_it_matters: By running an LLM locally on low‑power ESP32 devices, Tamagotchip enables on‑device AI planning and control without needing cloud connectivity, opening possibilities for privacy‑preserving and offline intelligent appliances.
